source.title: Exploring Task Performance with Interpretable Models via Sparse Auto-Encoders
source.authors: Shunyu Wang; Tyler Loakman; Youbo Lei; Yi Liu; Bohao Yang; Yuting Zhao; Dong Yang; Cheng-Hua Lin

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoders to decompose activations motivated by neuron polysemanticity, then applies its pipeline to downstream tasks. It does not measure neuron-pole job counts or test the claim versions about neurons. Its reported interpretability result concerns SAE features, not neurons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that more than 93% of GPT-4-generated SAE-feature interpretations were validated in unseen contexts, but does not report a neuron-level result or define a score comparable to the claim’s automated scoring version. Downstream task accuracy, SAE reconstruction loss, and sparsity do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders on four ~7B instruct LLMs and uses GPT-4 feature descriptions to reformulate prompts for math and metaphor tasks. It assumes neuron polysemanticity and superposition from prior work and never measures neuron-level interpretability shares, neuron explanation scores, attribution graphs or vision neurons. Its only interpretability number (>93% of SAE feature interpretations validated) concerns SAE features, not neurons. The rest is the method's own downstream performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE dictionary features expose LLM misinterpretations of mathematical symbols and metaphorical words. They also conclude that prompt reformulation guided by these features improves accuracy on MATH (+12.52 points average) and metaphor detection (+3.76 points average) across four ~7B models.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparse autoencoders to obtain dictionary features and uses those features in a downstream-task pipeline; it does not audit neuron poles or apply the original neuron-explanation audit method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study says it extracts activations from a middle-layer MLP block, typically layer 12 or 13, and that this choice was empirically selected for semantically coherent features; no claim-version outcome is reported across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: More than 93% of GPT-4 interpretations of 'interpretable' SAE features were reported validated in unseen contexts. This is an aggregate with no defined score and no per-model breakdown.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bills-style auto-interpretation of SAE features from middle-layer MLPs of ~7B LLMs validates for a large majority of features judged interpretable.

record.problems: The feature-validation result is reported only as an aggregate, with no definition of the validation score, model-specific breakdown, or uncertainty estimate; it concerns SAE features rather than neurons.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream math and metaphor accuracy, autoencoder reconstruction loss, and sparsity are not results about neuron interpretability or the claim versions, so they were not included.

untested.parts: No neuron-level interpretability shares in any model or across scale.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron re-analysis.
No comparison of neuron interpretability across architectures, regularization or tools.
No neuron-based attribution graphs or circuit explanations.
No test of whether activating-example explanations of neurons predict firing.
No simulation scores for neuron explanations. The SAE-feature validation is not comparable.

record.verdict_notes: Polysemanticity of neurons is asserted from cited work (Elhage 2022, Bricken 2023), not measured, so it gives no evidence against V1/V2. The reader's rows_left_out (downstream accuracy, reconstruction loss, sparsity) is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole shares in Qwen3-32B are not measured.
No neuron-pole interpretability shares across models or scales are measured.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or recursive-generalization account is tested.
No architecture/tool comparison or InceptionV1-sized vision-model interpretability estimates are tested.
No attribution graphs or neuron-based behavioral reconstruction are evaluated.
The study does not test whether neuron explanations that fit activating examples fail to predict neuron firing.
The reported validation concerns SAE-feature explanations, not neuron explanations; the paper does not report comparable automated scores for neuron explanations.

rows.subject: LLMs (aggregate across the four models named in the study)
rows.operation_detail: Validated GPT-4-generated SAE-feature interpretations in unseen contexts.
rows.measure: Share of interpretable SAE features whose GPT-4-generated interpretations were validated in unseen contexts with consistent precision.
rows.note: This is an aggregate result for SAE features, not neuron explanations. The paper does not define the validation score or give model-specific results.
rows.check: Concerns SAE dictionary features, not neurons. The score is undefined and the denominator ('interpretable features') is a pre-selected subset. It is the study's own method-quality check, not a measure of any version. Subject list: the text names 'Llama 3 (3.18B-Instruct)', likely a typo for 3.1 8B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
